blocks.text: Enter the world. Understand the evidence.
Explore the history, texts and languages behind the Bible, and weigh the evidence.
A world recorded. A past to investigate.
Begin with a historical question. Compare the biblical narrative with an ancient account, then examine the setting, source and limits of the comparison.
Learn how historians read archaeology and inscriptions through worked examples from the biblical world.
Open the museums themselves: real object records from collections that publish openly, with dates, findspots and photographs under their own licences.
Old maps of the Holy Land
Historical maps of the biblical world, 680 to 1928, from ten libraries. Open any map at full size, with its maker, its library and its credit.
Trace tribute, conquest, exile and return through synchronized maps and primary evidence.
Explore Jericho, Lachish, Jerusalem and Corinth through selected phases, finds and disputed interpretations.
The world of Jesus & the apostles
Explore eight connected settings, from Galilean households and Jerusalem to Caesarea, Corinth, Ephesus and travel toward Rome.
Mesha and the world of Moab
Illustrated landing for a historical study of Mesha and Moab.
Illustrated landing for a historical study of Lachish and the campaign.
Illustrated landing for a historical study of imperial restoration and return.
Follow rulers and their settings, then open the biblical passages and the people they connect.
Find a place and open the passages associated with it.
A surviving text, a modern edition and an interpretation each answer a different question.
Who made it, when, and for what purpose? Distinguish the ancient work from the copy or edition before you.
Follow the passage, its genre and the source’s own perspective. A royal inscription speaks with a royal purpose.
Separate what survives from the conclusions drawn from it. Compare interpretations and their supporting evidence.
Return to the passage and its teaching.
Rooted in Scripture. Open for discovery.
A place to read slowly, ask deeply, and follow the connections. Scripture, study and the voices of Christian history, brought together for a lifetime of learning.
A library with a paper trail.
Meet the authors. Explore the collection. Trace each work to its source.
